source.title: Unlocking the Address Book: Dissecting the Sparse Semantic Structure of LLM Key-Value Caches via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Qing-Sen Ma; Dian-Yun Wang; J. Lyu; Yaoye Wang; Lechen Ning; Sujie Zhu; Zhenbo Xu; Liu-Yu Xiang; Hui-Ning Li; Hui-Jia Wu; Zhao-Feng He

page_placements.theme: Fidelity depends on layer, activation site and decomposition method

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates Top-K SAE reconstructions of KV vectors, but it does not test the claimed structure or predictability of SAE error, token-level error overlap across SAE sizes, or the specified consequences of retaining the error term.
record.gate_note: The paper reports reconstruction-fidelity measurements and model performance under compressed KV reconstructions. These do not test the claim versions: it gives no linear prediction of the residual, token-level error comparison across SAE sizes, matched random-error comparison, separation of two error components, circuits or steering analysis, or controlled test of training-artifact explanations. Related reconstruction and performance results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: This is a KV-cache compression paper. It trains Top-K SAEs on Key/Value projections and reports cosine fidelity versus K and PPL/zero-shot accuracy under sparse reconstructions. It never isolates or analyses the SAE error vector: no linear prediction of the residual, no per-token error norms across SAE sizes, no matched random-error splice, no linear/nonlinear split, no circuits or steering with and without an error term, and no controlled architecture comparison. The Top-K choice is justified by citing shrinkage and dead latents, not tested. Its claim that discarded tail features are noise is asserted from its own compression results, not measured against the dark-matter versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right. Add that the authors propose a 'Denoising Hypothesis': features ranked beyond 8 are task-irrelevant noise, and dropping them can improve PPL. They recommend a dual budget (K=8 for Keys and shallow layers, K=16 for deep Values). The abstract lists Qwen2.5-32B, but no Qwen downstream results appear, only a fidelity curve.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies Top-K SAEs to Key and Value projections and measures reconstruction fidelity and downstream performance; it does not carry out the claim's residual-predictability, token-overlap, or matched-error analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction fidelity depends on vector type, layer, and sparsity budget K; deep Value vectors are reported to need a larger K than Keys and shallow Values.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-K SAE cosine fidelity on KV vectors depends on vector type, layer and inference K. Deep Values reach 0.658 at K=8 and 0.767 at K=16 (Yi-6B L30), while Keys exceed 0.8 at K=8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction fidelity on attention Key/Value projections is strongly role- and depth-dependent; deep Value vectors are less sparse-reconstructable than Keys.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse KV reconstructions at K=8 and K=32 give PPL equal to or slightly below the 'Dense (128)' reference across four models. Accuracy shifts are within about 1–2 points. No uncertainty is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Truncating Top-K SAE reconstructions of KV vectors to few latents does not degrade (and may slightly lower) perplexity relative to the K=128 reference; the authors' 'denoising hypothesis'.

record.problems: The reported reconstruction and downstream results do not isolate the SAE error term or compare it with matched random errors. No per-token residual statistics or error-context overlap across SAE sizes are reported. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates or statistical tests alongside the tabulated results.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted from the reported numeric reconstruction-fidelity points or Table 3 performance comparisons selected for fits_no_version.

untested.parts: All: no regression of the SAE residual on input activations.
All: no per-token error norms, no cross-size SAE comparison (only one expansion factor), no scaling of error.
All: no random-error baseline of matched norm; the spliced-versus-original loss comparison is unclear.
All: no decomposition of error into linear and nonlinear parts, no further dictionary learning on the residual.
All: no circuit or steering analysis, no error-term ablation.
All: Top-K is chosen on cited arguments about shrinkage and dead latents; no L1 versus Top-K or end-to-end comparison of error is run.

record.verdict_notes: The relation could equally be coded as unrelated; the paper does not cite the dark-matter source. All rows are the study's own compression method evaluated against its own reference. A single SAE size is used (expansion 32, Ktrain=32), trained on wikitext-2, and PPL is evaluated on wikitext-2. The text claims 'statistically insignificant' shifts but reports no statistical tests.

versions.untested_parts: No linear predictor of SAE error from input activations or measure of its explained share.
No per-token error norms, comparison of which tokens larger and smaller SAEs fail on, or evidence about whether error vanishes with SAE scale.
The study reports performance with SAE-reconstructed KV vectors, but does not compare against random errors of the same size.
No separation of linear and nonlinear error components or test of further dictionary learning on either component.
No circuits or steering analyses, or comparison of their results with and without an SAE error term.
No controlled comparison showing whether dark matter is mostly due to training objectives, shrinkage, dead latents, or architecture, or whether it shrinks with end-to-end training.

relation.reason: Discusses related reconstruction loss, shrinkage and information sufficiency, without testing or using the catalogued dark-matter findings.

tranche.reason: Measures KV reconstruction fidelity and downstream compression performance, without testing residual predictability, cross-SAE token errors, matched random errors, error-dependent analyses, or training-induced dark matter.

source_check.notes: The rows describe the study's own reconstruction method and budget selection, not evidence for V1–V6. Yi-6B L16 Key fidelity differs between §4.3 (approximately 0.81) and Figure 4's caption (over 0.86); §5.4's K=16 performance claims are not documented in Table 3, which lists K=8, 32 and 128.
